title: The manifest of one database snapshot (form 2)
description: Every snapshot the portal takes is a folder, web/_backups/upgrade-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS/, holding one file per table and this manifest, _manifest.json. The manifest is written LAST, under another name, and then renamed: so a folder that has a readable manifest is a finished snapshot, and a folder without one is a snapshot that failed, was cut off, or is still being taken, and must never be counted as a backup. Written and read by Portal\Core\DbBackup (web/_core/DbBackup.php). Checked, against a real sample, by tools/audit-checks/check_backup_column_types.py.
$comment: FOR MAINTAINERS. JSON has no comments, so every explanation lives here. This describes FORM 2, written since October 2026 (#577, #579). A manifest with no 'format' property at all is FORM 1, the older shape: one pretty-printed tblName.json per table, and only created_at, reason, php_version, mysql_server and, per table, columns, rows and sha256. Form 1 is still read and restored, but never written, and is not described by this schema. If the shape written ever changes, raise DbBackup::FORMAT, keep the old reader, run tools/backup-restore-selftest.php --write-samples to refresh the sample, and bring this file into line: the self-test compares the sample's property names with what the class writes today, and the check compares the sample with this schema, so the three cannot drift apart unnoticed. An older release refuses a snapshot whose format is higher than it knows.

format.description: Which form the snapshot's files are in. 2 today. A release that meets a higher number refuses the snapshot and changes nothing, because it cannot know what the newer form means.

created_at.description: The moment the snapshot was started, as a date, a time and the offset from UTC (for example 2026-10-12T07:48:19+00:00). Because it carries its offset it names one exact moment, which is what 'the newest snapshot' is decided by. The folder's name is only local clock time, and misleads on the night the clocks go back.

reason.description: A short label saying why the snapshot was taken: 'manual' from the Backup Management page, or 'pre-upgrade-' followed by the release number from the upgrade page.

php_version.description: The version of PHP that took the snapshot. For people investigating a problem; nothing acts on it.

mysql_server.description: The database server's own version text at the time. For people investigating a problem; nothing acts on it.

portal_version.description: The release of the portal that took the snapshot, or an empty text when it was taken by a tool that does not load the portal. The recovery guide reads this to find which release's code a snapshot belongs with.

time_zone.description: The time zone the database connection was set to while the snapshot was read, as an offset: always +00:00. A TIMESTAMP column holds a moment but is handed over as clock time in the connection's zone, so the zone has to be fixed and written down, and the restore sets the same one. Without this a snapshot moved by hours when restored on a host in another zone.

tables.description: One entry per table in the snapshot, keyed by the table's name. Only tables whose names start with tbl are copied.

unlisted_values.description: Values the snapshot found that are NOT on their column's list of choices, one entry for each column that holds any. Always present: an empty list means the snapshot looked and found none. A column with a list of choices (an ENUM), on a database set to accept anything, stores a value that is not on its list as an empty text and says nothing. A restore refuses such a value rather than change it, so a snapshot with anything in this list CANNOT BE PUT BACK WHOLE until those rows are mended in the live database and a new snapshot is taken. It is still good for looking at, and for putting back a single table that holds no such value. The backup page, the upgrade page and the health page all read this list and say so.
unlisted_values.$comment: FOR MAINTAINERS. Added on 12 October 2026, before form 2 was ever released, so every form 2 manifest a release writes has it and it is required here. The class still reads a manifest WITHOUT it (DbBackup::unlistedIn() then reports nothing), because a snapshot is never refused over a missing note; what cannot be told from such a manifest is whether anybody looked. A SET column is not looked at: the database drops a word that is not on a SET's list and keeps the rest, which goes back unchanged.

unlistedValue.description: One column holding values that are not on its list of choices.

table.description: The table the column is in.

column.description: The column, which has a list of choices (an ENUM).

cells.description: How many rows of the table held such a value in this column at the moment the snapshot was taken. Never 0: a column with none has no entry.

table.description: What the snapshot holds for one table.

columns.description: The table's columns, in the order their values appear in each row of its file. Columns the database works out for itself are left out, because they cannot be written back.

rows.description: How many rows the table's file holds. Compared with the file before a restore touches anything.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 checksum of the table's file, as 64 hexadecimal digits. A file that no longer matches has been changed, damaged or cut short since the snapshot was taken, and the restore refuses it.

file.description: The name of the table's file inside the snapshot folder: the table's name followed by .jsonl. Described by backup-table-file.schema.json.
